links.outcome: Accuracy and hallucination rates of LLMs with vs without retrieval-augmented grounding (Med-RISE)
links.effect: Med-RISE raised accuracy 9.8% to 16.3% (mean 13%) across 4 datasets and reduced hallucinations 11.8% to 18% (mean 15.1%); factuality hallucinations down 13.5%, faithfulness down 5.8%.
links.quote: The integration of Med-RISE with each LLM led to a substantial increase in accuracy, with improvements ranging from 9.8% to 16.3% (mean 13%, SD 2.3%) across the 4 datasets.

screen.practice: retrieval grounding with fact and safety output filter
screen.reason: The study tests the addition of a RAG framework with a fact and safety output filter (Med-RISE) to baseline LLMs and measures its impact on accuracy and hallucinations on benchmark medical QA datasets.

primary.practice: retrieval-augmented generation and output safety filtering
